_notes: First real content file for ARCHITECTURE.md section 3's component content shape (previously only illustrated as a fictional placeholder, component.buffer.overrun_patch). Ties docs/lore/corporations.md's Voss-Achebe Relay Systems (VARS) directly into existing gameplay content rather than leaving it as lore only. A VARS-MK2 buffer's hardware genuinely supports db/hardware/relay-courier-rig-class-c.json's rated duty_limit_pct_per_hour (10) -- the firmware caps it lower (4) unless a subscription check against a reachable licensing server passes. 'Degrading' one (Scrapshell slang for reflashing past the lock) is common enough to be referenced directly in docs/lore/os-lineages.md section 5.

subscription_gate.on_unreachable_licensing_server: falls back to locked_duty_limit_pct_per_hour, not rated -- fails closed, not open
subscription_gate._notes: the actual check mechanism is intentionally left engine/content-agnostic here -- how a node verifies subscription_current is a policy detail (ties to the tenant/namespace layer in ARCHITECTURE.md section 2), not something this component file should hardcode

installed_effect.degraded: reflashed firmware ignores subscription_gate entirely and applies rated_duty_limit_pct_per_hour instead

folklore: Scrapshell folk-knowledge: reflashing a VARS-MK2 to ignore its subscription check is common enough to have a name -- 'degrading' a buffer, ironic since the hardware performs better afterward. Not a scan-and-exploit action: it requires physical access and enough of RFC-2301's key-hierarchy knowledge (db/trust/rfc2301-key-hierarchy.json) to feed the firmware an update it accepts as legitimately signed.
